general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **US-China Summit:** US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Thursday, May 14, 2026, for two days of talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marking his first visit to the country since 2017 in his first term. During the summit, Xi warned that differences over Taiwan, which he called "the most important issue," could lead to conflict between the world's two largest economies, while both leaders agreed that the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for 20% of global gas, must remain open to support the free flow of energy. The White House stated that Trump and Xi also discussed trade, the Middle East, Ukraine, and the Korean Peninsula, and Beijing granted permission for hundreds of U.S. slaughterhouses to resume beef shipments to China ahead of the talks. The summit aimed to stabilize a crucial bilateral relationship amid heightened geopolitical tensions, including concerns over trade, regional conflicts, and the critical issue of Taiwan's sovereignty, impacting global economic stability and security.

• **Israel-Lebanon Conflict and Talks:** Israeli and Lebanese negotiators met in Washington D.C. on Thursday, May 14, 2026, for a third round of US-hosted talks aimed at ending the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah. Just before the talks, Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon struck seven vehicles, killing at least 12 people, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The Lebanese team was expected to push for an actual ceasefire, while Israel was likely to demand progress toward a Lebanese plan for disarming Hezbollah, with the current "ceasefire" set to expire on Monday. This escalating violence and stalled negotiations highlight the ongoing instability in the Middle East, which has significant implications for regional security, international diplomacy, and global energy markets.

• **Russia-Ukraine Conflict:** Russia launched a large daytime drone assault on Ukraine on Wednesday, May 13, 2026, killing at least six people and hitting multiple regions shortly after a three-day US-brokered ceasefire expired. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that at least 800 Russian drones had been launched since midnight and warned of potential missile attacks. The strikes targeted residential, railway, port, energy, and other civilian infrastructure across Ukraine, including regions near NATO borders, prompting Slovakia to close its land border crossings with Ukraine indefinitely for security reasons. This renewed escalation of hostilities underscores the fragility of ceasefires and the enduring threat to European security, impacting humanitarian efforts, regional stability, and international energy supplies.

• **US Humanitarian Aid:** The Trump administration announced on Thursday, May 14, 2026, an additional $1.8 billion in humanitarian funding for United Nations operations, bringing the total US support channeled through the UN-coordinated system to $3.8 billion following an earlier $2 billion allocation in December. UN Secretary-General António Guterres and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher welcomed the contribution, noting it would allow humanitarians to reach millions in urgent crises, even as UN agencies are "overstretched, under-resourced and literally under attack" and the US has cut overall foreign assistance. This funding is critical for addressing global humanitarian needs, estimated to affect 239 million people worldwide, amidst rising conflicts, displacement, and climate shocks, although the overall reduction in foreign aid from traditional donors signals a broader challenge for international relief efforts.

Why it matters: Today's top stories reflect a global landscape grappling with persistent geopolitical conflicts, the delicate balance of superpower relations, and the critical challenge of funding humanitarian crises amidst a reordering of international aid priorities.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Pacote de Benefícios Fiscais para a Habitação:** O Presidente da República promulgou em 12 de maio de 2026 um decreto-lei que visa estimular a oferta de habitação. Anteriormente, o IVA na construção residencial era de 23%, a taxa autónoma de IRS sobre rendimentos prediais era de 25%, e a dedução de rendas no IRS era de 700 euros. Agora, o IVA na construção residencial é reduzido para 6% para imóveis de "preço moderado" (até 660.000 euros para venda ou 2.300 euros/mês para arrendamento). A taxa de IRS sobre rendimentos de arrendamento de habitações a preço moderado baixa de 25% para 10%. Além disso, a isenção de mais-valias em IRS na venda de imóveis para habitação é aplicada quando o valor é reinvestido em imóveis destinados a arrendamento até 2.300 euros mensais. A dedução de rendas em sede de IRS para inquilinos aumenta de 700 euros para 900 euros. Esta medida pretende aumentar a oferta de habitação e aliviar a carga fiscal associada à compra e arrendamento de casa, aguardando apenas a publicação em Diário da República para produzir efeitos. [Executive Digest, The Portugal News, CASA SAPO Notícias]

• **Prorrogação da Moratória de Créditos por Fenómenos Meteorológicos:** O Presidente da República promulgou em 14 de maio de 2026 um decreto do Governo que estende por 12 meses a moratória de créditos para empresas, famílias e instituições sociais afetadas pelas tempestades do inverno. Anteriormente, a moratória de créditos teria um prazo final mais curto. Agora, permite o diferimento temporário do pagamento de capital, juros e outros encargos de empréstimos, bem como proíbe a revogação de linhas de crédito existentes. A medida visa estabilizar a tesouraria dos beneficiários e apoiar a retoma gradual da atividade económica nas zonas atingidas. [DN]

• **Alteração dos Encargos Plurianuais para Protocolos de Mediação Sociocultural da AIMA:** Foi publicada em Diário da República em 14 de maio de 2026 uma alteração ao diploma que autoriza a assunção dos encargos plurianuais e a realização da despesa para os protocolos de mediação sociocultural da Agência para a Integração, Migrações e Asilo (AIMA). Previamente, o encargo máximo total para 2026-2028 era inferior. Agora, o encargo máximo total para os anos de 2026 a 2028 é aumentado em 7.367.420,99 euros. Esta alteração assegura o financiamento necessário para a continuidade e expansão dos serviços de mediação sociocultural para migrantes. [Diário da República]

• **Adiantamento do Prazo de Entrega do Modelo 22 de IRC:** O Governo decidiu estender o prazo de entrega do Modelo 22 (Imposto sobre o Rendimento de Pessoas Coletivas – IRC). Anteriormente, o prazo-limite para a entrega do Modelo 22 era 31 de maio. Agora, o prazo foi alargado para 19 de junho de 2026. Esta prorrogação oferece mais tempo às empresas para o cumprimento das suas obrigações fiscais relativas ao IRC. [Economia e Finanças]

Why it matters: O pacote de benefícios fiscais para a habitação representa a mudança mais significativa, visando aumentar a oferta de casas e tornar o acesso à habitação mais acessível para cidadãos e empresas.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
Here is the EUROPEAN UNION POLICY section of your morning briefing:

• **Revised Directive on Package Travel and Linked Travel Arrangements:** Previously, the Directive (EU 2015/2302) governed package holidays. Now, the revised Directive, which formally entered into force on May 5, 2026, aims to remove legal uncertainties and strengthen consumer protection, especially in crisis situations. It simplifies definitions, abolishes the concept of linked travel arrangements, and ensures a more even distribution of responsibility among all participants in the travel chain. Member States, including Portugal, have until September 5, 2028, to transpose these changes into national legislation, with full application by March 5, 2029. This brings greater transparency and protection for travelers and requires travel businesses to adapt their practices and contracts.

• **Commission Guidance on EU Transport Sector amid Middle East Crisis:** Previously, general EU rules on air passenger rights and airline obligations applied. Now, guidance adopted on May 8, 2026, clarifies that high fuel prices are not considered "extraordinary circumstances" for airlines to avoid paying financial compensation for flight cancellations. Retroactive fuel surcharges added to airfares are also explicitly deemed impermissible. The guidance provides clarity on fuel uplift obligations, airport slots, and public service obligations, ensuring airlines maintain transparent upfront pricing. This ensures continued consumer protection for air passengers during disruptions and maintains clear obligations for airlines regarding pricing and compensation.

• **Agreement on AI Act Simplification Measures and Ban on "Nudifier" AI:** Previously, the original AI Act set compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems by August 2, 2026, and a six-month grace period for transparency obligations. Now, a provisional agreement reached on May 7, 2026, simplifies certain aspects to facilitate compliance for businesses. It includes an explicit ban on "nudifier" AI systems. The grace period for transparency obligations, such as watermarking AI-generated content, is reduced to three months, with a new compliance deadline of December 2, 2026. Providers must continue to register AI systems in the EU’s high-risk systems database, and the deadline for Member States to establish national AI regulatory sandboxes is postponed from August 2, 2026, to August 2, 2027. This streamlines compliance for businesses developing or deploying AI systems in the EU, while enhancing protection for citizens against harmful AI applications.

• **Directive Revising Lists of Pollutants in Surface and Groundwaters:** Previously, EU water quality monitoring relied on older lists of pollutants and primarily assessed individual pollutants. Now, the EU directive revising the lists of pollutants in surface and groundwaters entered into force on May 11, 2026. It requires Member States to monitor for an updated and expanded list of substances, including certain PFAS "forever chemicals," specific pesticides and pharmaceuticals, microplastics, and indicators of antimicrobial resistance. The directive also introduces "effect-based monitoring" to assess the combined risk to water quality, rather than solely individual pollutants, and streamlines some reporting obligations for Member States. This establishes stricter and more comprehensive environmental protection for EU water bodies, impacting industries that discharge pollutants and requiring updated monitoring by national authorities.

• **Regulation on the Protection of Adults in Cross-Border Situations:** Previously, adults needing protection in cross-border situations faced legal uncertainties regarding applicable jurisdiction and recognition of protective measures. Now, a political agreement reached on May 12, 2026, aims to establish harmonized rules across the EU on which court has jurisdiction, which law is applicable, and the recognition of protective measures or powers of representation in other Member States. It will introduce a European Certificate of Support and Representation to simplify proving powers in another Member State; formal adoption is imminent. This safeguards the rights and autonomy of adults with disabilities or health-related limitations when they move or reside across EU Member States, reducing administrative burden for their representatives, including carers, and is particularly relevant for Portuguese citizens with family members needing support across borders.

Why it matters: This week saw significant progress in consumer protection, particularly in travel and digital services, alongside strengthened environmental safeguards for water quality across the EU.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Notion:** Notion launched its Developer Platform on May 14, 2026, introducing "Workers" for custom code execution, an "External Agents API" to integrate third-party AI agents, and an "Agent SDK." This platform moves beyond Notion's existing Custom Agents by allowing external data syncing and complex multi-step automated workflows to run directly within the workspace, with Workers being free for developers through August 2026. A developer can now build an automated workflow to sync customer data from Salesforce into Notion databases nightly, making this information immediately actionable for Notion AI agents and team collaboration.

• **Perplexity:** Perplexity updated its "Computer" autonomous AI agent on May 14, 2026, with a focus on bringing advanced data science capabilities to every team. While "Personal Computer on Mac" launched earlier in May, this update expands Computer's ability to unify various AI capabilities for research, design, and data science tasks by leveraging 19 different AI models, including GPT-5.5 as the default orchestration model and GPT Image 2 for image generation. A knowledge worker can now use Perplexity Computer to quickly generate comprehensive data analyses from disparate sources and present them within team dashboards, effectively streamlining a multi-day research process into a single agentic workflow.

• **Samsung:** Samsung introduced its 2026 AI Television lineup on May 13, 2026, integrating new AI-powered features across its Micro RGB, OLED, Neo QLED, Mini LED, and Crystal UHD TVs. Key enhancements include "Vision AI Companion" (which integrates Bixby, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot), AI Upscaling Pro for real-time resolution enhancement, Colour Booster Pro for vivid colors, AI Football Mode Pro for optimized sports viewing, and AI Sound Controller Pro for adaptive audio. Consumers can now experience a more intelligent and personalized entertainment experience, where the TV proactively suggests content and optimizes viewing parameters based on real-time analysis, such as adjusting picture and sound for live sports.

Why it matters: The AI landscape is continuing its shift from foundational model releases to deeply integrated, agentic capabilities that enhance existing workflows and consumer experiences.

investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS

*   **Equities & Indices — Alphabet (Google):** Alphabet completed a record-breaking ¥576.5 billion ($3.6 billion) yen bond issuance, the largest ever by a foreign company in Japanese currency, to fund its significant artificial intelligence infrastructure expansion. This follows stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings, with EPS of $5.11 against an estimated $2.63 and revenue of $110 billion versus forecasts of $107 billion, driven by its cloud business. Pedro should note this as a strong signal of continued aggressive investment in AI infrastructure, reinforcing Alphabet's position in the AI race.
*   **Equities & Indices — Microsoft:** Competition regulators have launched a major antitrust investigation into Microsoft's bundling of products including Windows, Office, Teams, and Copilot AI, examining if these practices limit customer choice and competition. This probe could result in Microsoft being designated with "strategic market status," potentially leading to broader regulatory powers and new conduct requirements.
*   **Equities & Indices — Nvidia:** Nvidia stock reached a record $235.75, propelled by Wells Fargo raising its price target to $315 (implying 40% upside) and the US clearing approximately 10 Chinese firms to purchase Nvidia's H200 AI chip. CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly in Beijing to facilitate these stalled H200 chip sales, highlighting the company's efforts to unlock key international markets.
*   **Equities & Indices — Tesla:** Tesla is reportedly considering integrating GPUs directly into its vehicles, an early indication of accelerating its onboard compute roadmap beyond its existing custom chip strategy for advanced AI capabilities. Additionally, Tesla has removed Basic Autopilot from its online configurator in the Netherlands, pushing towards a subscription-only Full Self-Driving (FSD) model, with a deadline of May 15 for one-time FSD purchases in that market.
*   **Gold & Silver — Precious Metals:** Gold prices slipped due to a renewed risk-on sentiment ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing and a strengthening US dollar, which pressured bullion demand. Silver prices tumbled significantly, with MCX futures dropping 6%, as a war-driven surge in US inflation fueled expectations for higher interest rates and prompted speculators to take profits. Both metals faced headwinds from elevated energy prices stoking inflation concerns and expectations of prolonged high interest rates.
*   **Crypto — Bitcoin (BTC) & Ethereum (ETH):** Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $131 million on May 15, with BlackRock's IBIT leading with $144 million in inflows. Conversely, Ethereum spot ETFs experienced net outflows for the fourth consecutive trading day, totaling $5.65 million, as JPMorgan analysts suggest Ethereum and other altcoins may continue to underperform Bitcoin due to weaker network activity and fading confidence in the altcoin market. Institutional demand remains tilted toward Bitcoin, with its ETFs recovering faster after recent market turbulence.

Why it matters: Persistent institutional capital inflows into AI infrastructure and Bitcoin ETFs underscore a deepening bifurcation in market sentiment, favoring foundational tech and established digital assets over broader market diversification or lagging crypto alternatives.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Department of Justice Reschedules Certain Marijuana-Related Products:** On May 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) issued a final order that immediately moved certain marijuana-related products from Schedule I to Schedule III under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). This action applies to "drug products containing marijuana that have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)" and "marijuana subject to a state medical marijuana license." Previously, Schedule I drugs were considered to have no accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse; now, these specific products are classified as Schedule III, indicating accepted medical use and a lower potential for abuse, thereby legitimizing medical marijuana prescribed under state law and FDA-approved marijuana drugs under federal law. The DOJ also announced an expedited hearing, beginning June 29, 2026, to review broader rescheduling. This shift significantly impacts the legal landscape for cannabis businesses and medical research, potentially opening new investment opportunities in pharmaceutical and state-licensed medical marijuana sectors.

• **CFTC Eases Swap Reporting Requirements for Event Contracts:** On May 13, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's (CFTC) Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued a blanket no-action letter. This letter states that the CFTC will not recommend enforcement action against designated contract markets (DCMs), derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs), or their participants if they do not report fully collateralized event-contract transaction data to swap data repositories (SDRs) or meet related recordkeeping duties. Previously, these entities were generally subject to such reporting and recordkeeping obligations for event contracts that qualify as swaps; now, this regulatory relief reduces the compliance burden for prediction market operators. This action streamlines operations for platforms offering event contracts and could encourage further development in this niche financial market.

• **OFAC Publishes Sanctions Designations Targeting Cuban and Iranian Entities:** On May 14, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published a notice in the Federal Register detailing sanctions actions. This notice includes designations made on May 7, 2026, under Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which authorized the imposition of secondary sanctions on those responsible for repression in Cuba and for threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy. The notice also follows sanctions initiated on May 11, 2026, under E.O. 13224, targeting a network involved in selling Iranian oil for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and three senior officials. Previously, secondary sanctions against non-U.S. persons for Cuba-related business were not as explicitly defined, and specific Iranian oil networks were not designated; now, these individuals and entities are added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, blocking their property and prohibiting transactions with U.S. persons. These actions intensify economic pressure on Cuba and Iran, affecting international trade and companies with exposure to these regions or entities.

• **Department of Justice Files Complaint Against D.C. Bar Disciplinary Authorities:** On May 13, 2026, the Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a complaint against D.C. Disciplinary Counsel Hamilton P. Fox III, the D.C. Office of Disciplinary Counsel, and the D.C. Court of Appeals Board on Professional Responsibility. The complaint challenges their "improper use of bar discipline to regulate the official actions of Federal Government attorneys," seeking to nullify the D.C. Bar's prosecution of former Assistant Attorney General Jeff Clark. Previously, the D.C. Bar could pursue disciplinary actions against federal attorneys for their official conduct; now, the DOJ is asserting federal authority to prevent such probes into Executive Branch deliberations, potentially limiting the scope of state bar oversight over federal government lawyers. This action indicates a federal pushback against state-level oversight of federal legal counsel, potentially impacting future regulatory enforcement and litigation strategies involving government attorneys.

Why it matters: The most significant U.S. policy shift this week is the Department of Justice's final order to reschedule certain medical marijuana products, marking a pivotal change in federal drug classification that could profoundly impact the cannabis industry and related markets.

Takeaway: Pedro should prioritize evaluating Notion's new Developer Platform, specifically its "Workers" and "External Agents API," which shipped today and offer powerful, free automation capabilities for knowledge management and task automation until August 2026.
